command:
set -euo pipefail
EXPECTED_HTML=18770d8e333af1bc49a818da4dbd5c2e482b859e0142d0213df6c956184c931e
test "$(sha256sum buehne.html | awk '{print $1}')" = "$EXPECTED_HTML"
echo ===SOURCE===
grep -n -E 'KOPF_.*DATEI|KOPF_BILDER|kopf-schicht.*src|kopf_.*png|KOPF_ROLL' buehne.html | head -100
echo ===HEAD_ASSETS===
find kopf_rgba -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.png' -printf '%P %s\n' | sort | head -120
python3 - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
import glob, numpy as np, os, hashlib
expr=sorted(glob.glob('ausdruck_erweitert/*/*/frontal/stufe_00.png')); heads=sorted(glob.glob('kopf_rgba/**/*.png',recursive=True))
print('STUFE00_COUNT',len(expr),'HEAD_COUNT',len(heads))
# Find head assets matching 1536x1024; compare in broad eye region around measured mapped eye plate.
heads=[p for p in heads if Image.open(p).size==(1536,1024)]
print('HEAD_1536_COUNT',len(heads))
# Eye plate mapped region x476..891 y123..321; use wider search region to catch displaced/oversized expression eyes.
x0,y0,x1,y1=400,80,970,390
# Use first expression frame as a cheap nearest-head discovery, then aggregate against best candidates.
E=np.asarray(Image.open(expr[0]).convert('RGBA'),dtype=np.int16)
rank=[]
for p in heads:
 H=np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert('RGBA'),dtype=np.int16)
 # Compare only pixels where both are materially opaque in broad eye region.
 ea=E[y0:y1,x0:x1,3]>=128; ha=H[y0:y1,x0:x1,3]>=128; m=ea&ha
 if m.sum()<1000: continue
 d=np.abs(E[y0:y1,x0:x1,:3]-H[y0:y1,x0:x1,:3]).mean(axis=2)
 rank.append((float(d[m].mean()),p,int(m.sum())))
rank.sort(); print('NEAREST_HEADS',[(round(a,3),p,n) for a,p,n in rank[:12]])
# Report hashes of top candidates; a follow-up can use the exact source-selected one once source grep identifies it.
for a,p,n in rank[:5]: print('HEAD_SHA',p,hashlib.sha256(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest())
print('SCOPE=READ_ONLY_CANONICAL_HEAD_DISCOVERY')
PY
